description: Cybercrime complaints top 20,000 in Nepal, but only 155 arrests made  The Himalayan Times
publisher.title: The Himalayan Times
full_article:
KATHMANDU, AUGUST 14

Nepal Police registered 20,526 cybercrime-related complaints in fiscal year 2082/83 (mid-July 2025 to mid-July 2026), while only 161 cases were filed and 155 people arrested during the same period, according to the Central Police Newsroom.

Related Articles Case filed against eight individuals in Bal Mandir case; three arrested, five absconding Cybercrime cases explode in Dhading as complaints jump more than sixfold

The figure marks an increase from the previous two fiscal years; 18,926 complaints were registered in FY 2081/82 and 19,730 in FY 2080/81.

Among the complaints registered, misuse of Facebook and Messenger accounted for the largest share at 7,123, followed by TikTok at 6,776, WhatsApp at 3,105, Telegram at 1,031 and Instagram at 628. Email-related complaints numbered 114, alongside smaller numbers involving Viber (21), Imo (38), YouTube (64), WeChat (14), Twitter (11) and Google (11). Complaints linked to eSewa, Khalti, bank accounts and SMS totalled 744, while institution-related complaints numbered 846.

Cyber Bureau spokesperson, Police Senior Superintendent Dilip Kumar Giri, said misuse of social media has grown alongside its use. He said complaint patterns over the past two fiscal years show a rise in scams involving fraudsters posing as bank or wallet company representatives to access victims' accounts, as well as fraud through fake gift, lottery and parcel offers, romance scams, false promises of foreign employment, fake online job offers circulated via Telegram, WhatsApp and Instagram, and fraud disguised as online shopping.

Police said the changing nature of technology misuse has made criminal investigation increasingly challenging. The Cyber Bureau was established by a Government of Nepal decision on June 8, 2018, to prevent and investigate technology-related crime. Police said the bureau has since been strengthened with additional technological capacity, alongside programmes to build police personnel's cyber-crime and security expertise and to raise public awareness of cyber security.

title: Sher Bahadur Deuba Returns to Nepal After Five Months of Medical Treatment - Daily Pioneer
description: Sher Bahadur Deuba Returns to Nepal After Five Months of Medical Treatment  Daily Pioneer
publisher.title: Daily Pioneer
full_article:
Former prime minister Sher Bahadur Deuba returned to Nepal on Thursday after spending more than five months abroad for medical treatment following injuries sustained during the Gen Z protests last year.

Deuba and his wife, former foreign minister Arzu Rana Deuba, were seriously injured during violent protests on September 9, 2025, when anti-Government demonstrations led by the Gen Z movement swept across Nepal and resulted in the fall of the KP Sharma Oli Government. The couple travelled to Singapore in February for medical treatment. Deuba, who is also the former president of Nepali Congress (NC), reportedly stayed in Hong Kong for a brief period as well.

According to his party leaders, Deuba landed at Tribhuvan International Airport here in the afternoon after completing his medical treatment.

The whereabouts of Rana remain unclear. Deuba was received at the airport by senior NC leaders, including Purna Bahadur Khadka, Shashanka Koirala,

Prakash Man Singh and Bimalendra Nidhi, among others. Hundreds of party activists from across the country gathered near the airport to welcome the former prime minister, cheering as he arrived.

In an appeal issued after his arrival, Deuba said the mountains, green hills and vast plains of the Tarai had called him back home.

The former premier said he has returned not as a leader but as a lifelong citizen of the nation, ready to serve with humility, dedication, and love.

Deuba, 80, has served as Nepal’s prime minister five times between 1995 and 2022 and is a veteran NC leader. He became party president in 2016 and was re-elected in 2021. During the Gen Z protest, Deuba was not holding any ministerial position. He was serving as a Member of Parliament and the party president.

title: Exclusive: ISI role suspected in Nepal riots; funds routed via Pak, Turkey, Qatar - India Today
description: Exclusive: ISI role suspected in Nepal riots; funds routed via Pak, Turkey, Qatar  India Today
publisher.title: India Today
full_article:
After years of continued diabolical terror plots in India, Pakistan now seems to be attempting to disturb peace in the neighbouring Nepal as the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) is suspected to have played a covert role in the communal riots that recently erupted in Sunsari district along the India border, exclusive details accessed by India Today show.

Investigators are examining evidence that illegal funds were routed into Nepal through networks linked to Pakistan, Turkey and Qatar. The findings form part of a preliminary report submitted by Nepal’s National Investigation Department (NID) to the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The unrest began on July 26 in Kaptanganj in Sunsari district, which borders Bihar and is an important transit corridor between India and Nepal.

Authorities said clashes broke out between two communities during separate religious programmes over the use of loudspeakers and the display of religious flags.

According to the NID report, a Turkey-based cleric of Pakistani origin, Mohammad Ilyas Ghuman, had stayed for several days at a mosque in Dewanganj before the violence.

He was accompanied by Mufti Abu Bakr Qasmi, the Imam of Kathmandu’s Jama Masjid. Investigators are examining whether their presence and meetings with local clerics in border districts had any connection with the subsequent unrest.

The report says Islamic flags had been erected around a vacant plot associated with a Shiva temple in Kaptanganj during Muharram observances. Local Hindu residents had reportedly sought their removal for weeks before the violence.

On the night before a Shravan pilgrimage ritual, a group of Kanwariyas was allegedly attacked near a madrasa, triggering wider clashes. The NID has also identified a local electricity department employee, Naseem Ansari, as the person who disconnected power supply in the area shortly before the attack.

Security forces later opened fire while attempting to control the violence. Official figures indicate more than a dozen people were injured, while local residents have claimed the number was higher.

The NID report describes Ghuman as a prominent member of the banned Tablighi Jamaat and alleges links to organisations such as Harkat-ul-Mujahideen, Harkat-ul-Ansar and Hizbul Mujahideen, all of which are banned in India and several other countries.

Nepalese investigators are now probing whether his movements through Biratnagar, Rautahat, Nepalgunj and Kapilvastu were linked to meetings held in mosques and madrasas in those districts.

Investigators are also examining the presence of nine Bangladeshi clerics who arrived in Kathmandu from Dhaka via Kuala Lumpur on July 20 on 30-day tourist visas and later travelled through districts bordering India.

The report has revived concerns about Nepal being used as a base for activities directed against India.

Security officials note that the ISI was highly active in Nepal during the 1990s and early 2000s and that the 1999 Indian Airlines hijacking had exposed the use of Nepalese territory for anti-India operations.

Indian agencies have also flagged several recent cases involving Nepal-based networks.

These include the arrest of Nepali national Prabhat Kumar Chaurasia in Delhi in 2025 in an alleged SIM card supply module linked to the ISI, the arrest of Ansarul Miyan Ansari with sensitive military-related material, and the detention of Sheikh Salim in Nepal in connection with an alleged ISI-linked arms network.

Nepalese investigators are also reviewing the case of four Pakistani nationals arrested in Kapilvastu in April 2026, which some security officials believe may have had intelligence links.

Another area of concern for both Nepal and India is the rapid growth of mosques and madrasas in border districts.

Official Nepalese data show about 911 registered institutions in areas adjoining India, while authorities estimate that roughly 3,000 more remain unregistered along the 1,751-km open border.

Investigators say a substantial share of foreign funding originates from countries including Turkey, Qatar, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

The preliminary intelligence findings are now expected to lead to a wider investigation into funding channels, cross-border networks and the role of foreign clerics in Nepal’s recent communal unrest, with both Nepalese and Indian security agencies closely monitoring developments along the sensitive border belt.

रिपोर्ट म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि मुहर्रम केरऽ उत्सव के दौरान कपतानगंज केरऽ एगो शिव मंदिर स॑ जुड़लऽ खाली भूखंड के आसपास इस्लामी झंडा लगैलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । बताओल जा रहल अछि जे स्थानीय हिन्दू निवासी हिंसा सं पहिने हफ्ता भरि सं हुनका सभ के हटाबय के मांग केने छल.

श्रावण तीर्थ संस्कार सं पहिने राति मे एकटा मदरसा के पास कांवरिया के एकटा समूह पर कथित तौर पर हमला भेल छल जाहि सं व्यापक झड़प भ गेल छल. एनआईडी न॑ स्थानीय बिजली विभाग केरऽ एगो कर्मचारी नसीम अंसारी क॑ भी वू व्यक्ति के रूप म॑ पहचान करलकै जे हमला स॑ कुछ देर पहलें इलाका म॑ बिजली आपूर्ति क॑ काटै वाला छेलै ।

बाद मे सुरक्षा बल हिंसा पर काबू लगेबाक प्रयास मे गोली चला देलक। आधिकारिक आंकड़ा बता रहल अछि जे एक दर्जन सं बेसि लोक घायल भेल अछि, जखन कि स्थानीय निवासी के दावा अछि जे ई संख्या एहि सं बेसि छल.

एनआईडी केरऽ रिपोर्ट म॑ गुमान क॑ प्रतिबंधित तबलीगी जमात केरऽ प्रमुख सदस्य बतैलऽ गेलऽ छै आरू हरकत-उल-मुजाहिदीन, हरकत-उल-अंसार आरू हिजबुल मुजाहिदीन जैसनऽ संगठनऽ स॑ संबंध के आरोप लगैलऽ गेलऽ छै, जे सब प॑ भारत आरू कई अन्य देशऽ म॑ प्रतिबंध छै ।

विराटनगर, रौतहट, नेपालगंज आ कपिलवस्तु के माध्यम सं हुनकर आवागमन ओहि जिला के मस्जिद आ मदरसा मे आयोजित बैसार सं जुड़ल छल कि नहि से आब नेपाली अन्वेषक जांच क रहल छथिन्ह.

जांचकर्ता 30 दिनक पर्यटन वीजा पर 20 जुलाई कए ढाका स कुआलालंपुर होइत काठमांडू पहुंचल आ बाद मे भारत क सीमावर्ती जिला स गुजरल नौटा बांग्लादेशी मौलवी क उपस्थिति क जांच सेहो क रहल अछि।

रिपोर्ट स नेपाल कए भारत क खिलाफ निर्देशित गतिविधि क आधार क रूप मे उपयोग कैल जेबाक चिंता फेर स जागि गेल अछि।

सुरक्षा अधिकारी सब नोट करै छै कि आईएसआई 1990 के दशक आरू 2000 के दशक के शुरुआत के दौरान नेपाल में बहुत सक्रिय छेलै आरू 1999 के इंडियन एयरलाइंस के अपहरण के बाद भारत विरोधी अभियान के लेलऽ नेपाली इलाका के उपयोग के खुलासा होय गेलऽ छेलै ।

भारतीय एजेंसी नेपाल स्थित नेटवर्क सं जुड़ल हाल के कईटा मामला के सेहो झंडा देखा देलक अछि.

एहि मे आईएसआई सं जुड़ल कथित सिम कार्ड सप्लाई मॉड्यूल मे 2025 मे दिल्ली मे नेपाली नागरिक प्रभात कुमार चौरसिया के गिरफ्तारी, अंसारुल मियाँ अंसारी के संवेदनशील सैन्य संबंधी सामग्री के संग गिरफ्तारी, आ आईएसआई सं जुड़ल कथित हथियार संजाल के सिलसिला मे नेपाल मे शेख सलीम के हिरासत मे लेल गेल शामिल अछि.

विज्ञापन

नेपाली जांचकर्ता अप्रैल २०२६ म॑ कपिलवस्तु म॑ गिरफ्तार करलऽ गेलऽ चार पाकिस्तानी नागरिकऽ के मामला के समीक्षा भी करी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ कुछ सुरक्षा अधिकारी सिनी के मानना छै कि खुफिया संबंध भी होय सकै छै ।

नेपाल आ भारत दुनूक लेल एकटा आओर चिंता के क्षेत्र अछि सीमावर्ती जिला मे मस्जिद आ मदरसा के तेजी सं बढ़ब.

नेपाली आधिकारिक आंकड़ा भारत स सटल इलाका मे करीब 911 पंजीकृत संस्था बता रहल अछि, जखन कि अधिकारी क अनुमान अछि जे 1,751 किलोमीटर क खुला सीमा पर लगभग 3,000 आओर अपंजीकृत अछि।

जांचकर्ता के कहना छै कि विदेशी फंडिंग के काफी हिस्सा तुर्की, कतार, कुवैत, सऊदी अरब आरू संयुक्त अरब अमीरात सहित देशऽ स॑ मिलै छै ।

खुफिया जानकारी केरऽ प्रारंभिक निष्कर्ष स॑ अब॑ फंडिंग चैनल, सीमा पार स॑ नेटवर्क आरू नेपाल केरऽ हाल केरऽ साम्प्रदायिक अशांति म॑ विदेशी मौलवी के भूमिका के व्यापक जांच के उम्मीद छै, जेकरा म॑ नेपाली आरू भारतीय सुरक्षा एजेंसी दोनों ही संवेदनशील सीमा पट्टी के साथ-साथ घटनाक्रम प॑ बारीकी स॑ नजर रखी रहलऽ छै ।

full_article:
Nepali youths, joined by former Gorkha soldiers and their family members, took to the streets in Nepal's Pokhara city this week, demanding Nepalese citizens be allowed to enlist as Agniveers under the Indian Army's Agnipath scheme. The enlistment of Gorkha soldiers into the Indian Army has been one of the strongest shared links between India and Nepal.

But recruitments have been paused since 2019, initially due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Nepal subsequently suspended the recruitment of Nepali youths after India introduced the Agnipath scheme in 2022, under which only up to 25 per cent of recruits are retained for permanent service after four years.

The remaining 75 per cent are discharged with a one-time lump-sum payment and do not receive pensions or other long-term career benefits.

The Nepali government had halted the recruitment, arguing that the scheme was inconsistent with the provisions of the 1947 Tripartite Agreement between India, Nepal, and Britain.

Why Nepali Youth Is Protesting

The protests in Pokhara come ahead of Indian Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth's scheduled visit to Nepal on Sunday.

With employment opportunities in Nepal limited, many young people in the Himalayan nation are interested in joining the Indian Army under the Agnipath scheme and are urging the Balendra (Balen) Shah government in Kathmandu to resume the recruitment process.

The protest march in Pokhara, a major tourism city in western Nepal, was organised by the Indian Ex-Servicemen Gorkha Brigade Nepal and was attended by former soldiers, their family members and youths who had received training to join foreign armies.

The protesters carried placards demanding the resumption of recruitment of Nepali youths under the revamped recruitment Agnipath scheme introduced by the Indian government.

The Demands

They said Nepali youths should be allowed to join the Indian Army as Agniveers rather than being compelled to seek employment in Gulf countries, according to a report by news agency IANS.

Among their key demands, which they also shared on social media, protesters asked for immediate reopening of the Agnipath recruitment process, which they said was essential to protect employment opportunities for Nepali youths and preserve the identity and tradition associated with Gurkha soldiers.

The protesters also demanded that the registration process for organisations representing former soldiers and bearing the term "ex-servicemen" not be halted. Such organisations, they said, are necessary to safeguard the dignity, rights and interests of former soldiers.

The rally, which began at Pokhara Stadium, proceeded to the District Administration Office, where the organisers submitted a memorandum to the Chief District Officer of Kaski in the presence of a large gathering.

नेपालक पोखरा शहरमे नेपाली युवक पूर्व गोरखा जवान आ हुनक परिवारक सदस्यसभ एहि सप्ताह सड़क पर उतरि भारतीय सेनाक अग्निपथ योजना अन्तर्गत नेपाली नागरिकके अग्निवीरके रुपमे भर्ती हेबाक अनुमति देबाक माँग केलक अछि । गोरखा जवान के भारतीय सेना में भर्ती भारत आ नेपाल के बीच सबस मजबूत साझा कड़ी में स एक रहल अछि।

मुदा 2019 स भर्ती रोकल गेल अछि, शुरू मे कोविड-19 महामारी क कारण। एकरऽ बाद भारत न॑ २०२२ म॑ अग्निपथ योजना शुरू करला के बाद नेपाल न॑ नेपाली युवा सिनी के भर्ती प॑ रोक लगाय देलकै, जेकरा तहत ४ साल बाद मात्र २५ प्रतिशत तलक भर्ती होय वाला क॑ स्थायी सेवा लेली बरकरार रखलऽ जाय छै ।

शेष 75 प्रतिशत कें एक बेर कें एकमुश्त भुगतान सं छुट्टी देल जायत छै आ ओकरा पेंशन या अन्य दीर्घकालिक कैरियर लाभ नहि भेटैत छै.

नेपाली सरकार भारत, नेपाल, ब्रिटेन के बीच १९४७ के त्रिपक्षीय समझौता के प्रावधान के साथ असंगत ई तर्क दैत भर्ती रोकने छल ।

Key Takeaways:

Dhangadhi/Nepalgunj forecast 36–38°C, Bhairahawa also up to 38°C

Very heavy rainfall likely in Karnali and Sudurpashchim hilly regions

Kathmandu cloudy with moderate rain, 28–30°C daytime

Pokhara 30–32°C with 60% chance of rain

Western Nepal is set for a sharp weather contrast on Friday, with Dhangadhi and Nepalgunj forecast to reach up to 38°C while parts of Karnali and Sudurpashchim face the possibility of very heavy rainfall.

The Meteorological Forecasting Division said generally cloudy conditions would prevail across the country, with moderate rain accompanied by thunder and lightning expected across large parts of the Himalayan, hilly and Terai regions.

Very heavy rainfall is likely at one or two places in the Himalayan and hilly regions of Karnali and Sudurpashchim provinces. Heavy rain is also possible in parts of Koshi, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces.

Among the major cities, Dhangadhi and Nepalgunj are forecast to record maximum temperatures of 36–38°C, while Bhairahawa is also expected to reach 36–38°C. Janakpur could reach 35–37°C and Simara 35–37°C.

In Kathmandu, moderate rain with thunderstorms is forecast, with temperatures ranging from 28–30°C. Pokhara is expected to record 30–32°C with a 60% chance of rain.

The weather office said the monsoon is currently influencing the entire country. The monsoon low-pressure line is around its average position in the eastern parts and lies slightly north of its average position near Nepal in the western parts.

For tonight, moderate rain or snowfall with thunderstorms is possible in parts of the Himalayan and hilly regions, while heavy rainfall is likely at one or two places in the hilly regions of Bagmati, Gandaki, Karnali and Sudurpashchim.

publisher.title: The New Indian Express
full_article:
At least three 'kanwariyas' from Nepal, including a 10-year-old boy, were killed and 10 others injured after a bus carrying pilgrims rammed into a stationary truck in Jharkhand’s Koderma district on Friday, police said.

The accident occurred at Pokhradih in the Satgawan police station area at around 4.30am, an officer said.

“At least three 'kanwariyas' were killed and 10 others were injured in the accident. The injured have been admitted to a local hospital,” Satgawan police station in-charge Bablu Kumar told PTI.

publisher.title: The Himalayan Times
full_article:
KATHMANDU, AUGUST 13

Media researcher Umesh Pokharel has been elected as the new chair of Media Action Nepal, following a meeting of the organisation's executive committee members in Kathmandu today.

Related Articles Investing in the next generation: A lesson for Nepal and the world The new Vice Chancellor of TU: A defining test for Nepal's higher education

Pokharel is a media activist and researcher with extensive experience in the media and development sectors. He previously served as South Asia Coordinator of the International Federation of Journalists (IFJ) and has also worked as a research consultant for DW Akademie, Germany. His background spans media research, journalism, media development, press freedom and journalists' rights, with a particular focus on South Asia.

Assuming office, he said, "I am pleased to be part of Media Action Nepal and to contribute to its mission, vision, goals and priorities, particularly in promoting freedom of expression, journalists' safety, the right to information, and media development."
